findings.claim: Canonical finalization can be authorized by forged gitignored mirror receipts.
findings.analysis: The contract declares git notes authoritative, but the checker falls back to .svc receipt mirrors whenever no note exists and completion consumers do not reject mirror-sourced success. The emitter also merges every mirror entry into the canonical note without validating those sibling entries. A locally fabricated verify-promotion mirror can therefore pass Stop/final-report or be promoted into durable notes during an unrelated legitimate emission.
findings.proposed_fix: Require note-sourced envelopes for stop, verify-promotion, final-report, push, and reconcile consumers. Never merge mirror contents into notes; regenerate mirrors only from validated notes.

findings.claim: External dispatch silently remaps Cursor, Grok, and other non-Codex/non-AGY hosts to the Claude binary.
findings.analysis: The launcher selects Codex and AGY explicitly, then routes every other host through Claude CLI arguments. Owner policy can name host=cursor, yet the recorded tuple remains Cursor while the executed binary is Claude. This defeats dispatch provenance and violates AC-551-7/AC-546-6.
findings.proposed_fix: Use an explicit host-to-transport registry. Invoke the exact declared transport or return capability_limited; reject unknown hosts instead of using an else-to-Claude branch.

findings.claim: Grok continuation records a successful launch although no process is launched.
findings.analysis: Grok declares fresh_session_launch enabled but launch_command is null. Non-fake launch skips spawn when the command is absent and still appends launch_receipted with pid=null. Reconcile then treats it as already launched forever. The live fixture invokes grok -p separately and does not exercise this controller path.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat enabled-without-launch_command as capability_limited. Require confirmed process creation before launch_receipted and test the real controller launch path.

findings.claim: Continuation consumption accepts contradictory or cross-WI evidence as a passing closeout.
findings.analysis: Consumption never verifies result.wi against the baton WI and does not require event_status=success, all AC mappings to pass, or substantive artifacts. A result with event_status=failure and verdict=pass closes as closed_pass solely from verdict.
findings.proposed_fix: Bind WI, session, launch token, and result digest; require event_status=success, verdict=pass, no failing AC mappings, and required evidence artifacts before closed_pass.

findings.claim: The continuation phase guard fails open when its ledger is corrupt or unreadable.
findings.analysis: Any exception during baton lookup exits successfully, allowing the continuation child to invoke forbidden planning or execution skills. This contradicts the mechanical-denial requirement in AC-552-4.
findings.proposed_fix: Fail closed for sessions identified as continuation children when ledger validation fails, with an explicit recovery blocker.

findings.claim: Cursor and Grok Stop adapters convert core-guard execution failures into success.
findings.analysis: Both adapters discard stderr and apply `|| true` around the core guard. Missing scripts, crashes, or malformed empty output consequently reach the unconditional exit 0 path.
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve the core exit status and require schema-valid allow output. Any execution or parse failure must emit a compact blocker and exit 2.

findings.claim: A caller can forge the repository-owner session-override receipt and replace owner dispatch policy.
findings.analysis: Overrides and receipts may be supplied as inline JSON. Receipt validation only checks self-asserted strings, optional expiry, and session/WI values; it neither authenticates owner issuance nor binds the receipt to the override digest. A session can fabricate authority=repository-owner and remap its own execution.
findings.proposed_fix: Require a protected owner-created receipt that binds the exact override SHA-256, WI, session, issue time, and expiry, with independently verifiable owner authorization.

findings.claim: A WI-scoped dispatch overlay leaks whenever the caller omits the current WI.
findings.analysis: Scope mismatch is enforced only when both overlay.scope.wi and a caller WI are present. If WI resolution is absent, the scoped overlay applies globally and can silently remap another workflow.
findings.proposed_fix: Reject a scoped overlay when the current WI is unavailable, and require explicit scope for work overlays.

findings.claim: The requested examined SHA is not a valid frozen revision.
findings.analysis: The supplied SHA is 38 hexadecimal characters and does not resolve. Repository HEAD and the self-review identify the actual 40-character SHA as 5a95ab3c9db00730862771fcd7f7e9aa4a119454, which is the revision examined here.
findings.proposed_fix: Bind all review and receipt artifacts to the actual 40-character HEAD SHA and correct the frozen-range metadata before release.
